jordan-cs: Customer acme-prod hit 403 on both /v1/generate and /v1/embeddings after a key rotation. They say requests used to work, started failing right after we rolled a new svc token. Request id: r-0a1b2c3d. Posting curl they ran:

jordan-cs: ```bash
curl -i -H \"Authorization: Bearer svc_XXX_NEW\" \"https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate\" -d '{\"input\":\"hello\"}'
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
{\"error\":\"insufficient_permissions\", \"message\":\"missing scope: generation\"}
```

mike-infra: Can you share the decoded token claims (redact kid/key) or the exact provisioning flow used? suspect provisioner trimmed something during CSV upload or the ingress mutated the scope list.

jordan-cs: Customer attached token-decoded output: `{"sub":"svc-acme","scopes":"embeddings"}` — only embeddings present. They say the UI showed both embeddings + generation checked when they created the key.

nisha-eng: Hmm. That looks like a scope-serialization mismatch. Provisioner historically accepts comma-separated scopes. But some proxies (looking at past bugs) rewrite headers or convert spaces to `+` and then our parser splits on whitespace only, so final claim becomes single token.

alex-plat: Repro steps request: jordan, can you ask customer to run this quick curl and paste the response headers (we need the raw Authorization header as it arrives to us)?

jordan-cs: Sent repro to customer with small script. They responded with their gateway logs showing header: `Authorization:Bearer svc_XXX_NEW` (no space after colon) and their CSV export that provisioner consumed shows `embeddings generation rerank` (space-separated). They say they uploaded via SAML-provisioner CSV.

mike-infra: Aha. SAML-provisioner import uses comma joiner in our code path, but CSV with space-separated scopes ends up as a single field with spaces. Our claim normalizer currently splits on commas only. So if the CSV used spaces, we didn't split and put the whole string into the `scopes` claim — but our downstream token encoder rewrites it incorrectly, resulting in only the first scope being recognized.

nisha-eng: Quick patch option: normalize on whitespace and commas when building token claims. I can prepare a hotfix for the provisioner for today.

ops-bot: incident created: INC-2026-1147 - svc token provisioning produced single-scope tokens for some CSV imports. Severity: P2. Affected tenants: small subset using manual SSO csv import (est ~4).

mike-infra: For immediate customer mitigation, re-provision a new key via the UI (UI uses multiselect and will write comma-separated scopes). If they can't, create an org-level fallback key with both generation+embeddings and rotate them to it.

jordan-cs: Customer accepted creating a temporary org key. They asked for exact command to test both endpoints. Pasting test they ran after we created fallback key:

jordan-cs: ```bash
# test generation
curl -s -H \"Authorization: Bearer org_fallback_ABC\" -d '{\"input\":\"test\"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate | jq .status
200
# test embeddings
curl -s -H \"Authorization: Bearer org_fallback_ABC\" -d '{\"input\":\"test\"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings | jq .status
200
```

jordan-cs: They confirmed both returned 200 and content looks normal. :tada:

nisha-eng: I'm pushing a small change to provisioner to split scopes on `/[ ,]+/` and to trim tokens. Will also add a migration to re-emit tokens for recent CSV imports within the last 48h.

alex-plat: Once deployed, we should re-provision affected tokens and notify customers. Also add a short doc blurb about accepted scope delimiters in SAML CSV.

mike-infra: Change is deployed to staging. Nisha, can you schedule a canary to prod with a short window? ops-bot, please run the migration plan.

ops-bot: migration job queued: MIG-3501 — will re-encode tokens for 6 tenants in rolling batches over 30m.

nisha-eng: Canary deployed to prod — no errors in 10m. Starting migration now.

oncall-bot: Alert: 2 customer transactions retried, latency unchanged. No new 403 spikes detected post-migration.

jordan-cs: Customer confirmed they replaced old svc_ key with the new UI-generated key and all their embedded pipelines resumed. They want a short explanation for their security team; I sent: \"During CSV-based SSO provisioning, space-separated scopes were not normalized by the provisioner which led to a single combined scope value in the token claim. We patched the provisioner to accept spaces and commas and re-provisioned affected tokens.\"

alex-plat: Addendum for postmortem: include repro, root cause (CSV delimiter mismatch + provisioner parser), mitigation (UI fallback + hotfix), and follow-ups (docs + stricter validation).

jordan-cs: Thanks everyone — I'll close the customer loop and mark the incident resolved once migration completes. :white_check_mark:

mike-infra: Nice work.

jordan-cs: closing now, will file a short postmortem doc link in the incident ticket.
